body_markdown:
This series is about history as found during[my travels](https://www.murileemartin.com/JunkyardGalleryHome.html) in the car graveyards of the world. Most of the time, that means just automotive ** history with the occasional digression into industry-altering geopolitical events, but today’s FPS subject gives us a look into *music* history as well.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


I found this truck at my favorite Front Range Colorado boneyard:[Speedway Auto Wrecking](https://murileemartin.substack.com/p/gm-and-chrysler-iron-at-colorados) in Dacono. The mountain peaks to the west that form this yard’s beautiful backdrop are 13,911-foot[Mount Meeker](https://www.14ers.com/peaks/10136/13er-mount-meeker) in the center, with 14,259-foot[Longs Peak](https://www.nps.gov/romo/planyourvisit/longs_peak_conditions_report.htm) just visible behind it and to the right.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


To the east, the Great Plains stretch all the way to Missouri. If you want to visit Speedway, be aware that it’s only open on Saturday mornings. Wear good boots.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


I’d seen this Dodge in a truck-centric section of Speedway for many years, and the “Freddi-Henchi Band” livery didn’t ring a bell with me (because I’ve only lived in Colorado for 16 years). I’d assumed it was the gear-hauler for some long-forgotten bar band from, say, Amarillo or Tulsa.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Then, on a recent Speedway trip, I happened to notice this **BOULDER COLO** lettering and decided to do some research.


And, oh man, did I regret not looking up the name on this Tradesman earlier! The Freddi & Henchi Band was one of the biggest musical acts in the Boulder-Denver region during the 1970s and 1980s.


Not only that, the influence of[the bands featuring Fred “Love” Gowdy and Marvin “Henchi” Graves](https://cmhof.org/inductees/freddi-henchi/) goes well beyond just northeastern Colorado. Do you like[the music of Earth, Wind & Fire](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zu9a29UR2dU) ? You can thank these guys for inspiring their sound in the mid-to-late 1960s.


Freddi-Henchi and the Soul Setters[got their start in Phoenix](https://cmhof.org/music-news/celebrating-black-history-month-an-interview-with-freddi-gowdy/) , Arizona, in 1966. They began as a cover band performing songs by artists such as James Brown and Smokey Robinson, then moved on to composing their own material. They relocated to Los Angeles in 1968, developed a following in California, and got regular work touring the country with acts such as Three Dog Night, Steely Dan, and Chicago.


A two-week gig in Fort Collins, Colorado, in 1970 led to the band moving to Boulder, a hard-partying college town with (at the time) cheap housing. Their funk/soul/R&B/rock sound proved popular, and[they became a Boulder institution](https://www.dailycamera.com/2023/07/16/in-retrospect-beloved-boulder-band-freddi-and-henchi-shaped-the-70s-scene/) for the entire decade and well into the next one, becoming known as the Crown Princes of Funk.


The era exacted a harsh toll on musicians. A couple of members of the Freddi-Henchi Band died during the 1970s, one in a car crash on US Highway 36 and the other from a heroin overdose. Freddi was drinking hard as the 1980s dawned while Henchi developed a cocaine problem, finally quitting the band in 1984 and ending up in jail later in the decade.[The two reunited in the mid-1990s](https://www.westword.com/music/back-from-the-grave-5054972/) , though, and kept playing together until Henchi[died of cancer in 2009](https://5280.com/marvin-henchi-graves-dies/) .


The good news is that Freddi Gowdy is still alive and well. He has been[performing with Chris Daniel & the Kings](https://www.lhvc.com/story/2026/07/08/news/chris-daniels-andamp-the-kings-with-freddi-gowdy-returns-to-rock-andamp-rails/12228.html) for quite a few years now and gets the job done. There’s a lot of history in the junkyard, if you know where to look.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The rear license plate on this van shows a[Boulder County MS code](http://www.15q.net/coco.html) . The final registration expired in late 1989, from the era soon after Henchi left the band.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Since the band probably bought the van new in 1976 and the inside of the cargo box shows the battle scars of countless amplifiers and equipment cases, we can assume it could tell some amazing stories from its 13 years of working gigs all over the Front Range plus the ski towns in the mountains.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


It was bought new from the[Hollister Motor Company in Boulder](https://localhistory.boulderlibrary.org/islandora/object/islandora%3A23239) .


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Its date of manufacture was June of 1976, just a month before[the Bicentennial of the United States of America](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s8_Rm3lPEfY) . The build tag tells us that it was assembled at[Warren Truck Assembly](https://media.fcanorthamerica.com/newsrelease.do?id=343&mid=8) as a B300 one-ton “Kary-Van” cab-and-chassis and fitted with a 360-cubic-inch two-barrel V-8 engine. Hollister Dodge must have had the cargo box added by a local business.


Chrysler Corporation


Dodge’s use of the Tradesman name began with the first generation of Chrysler’s small vans:[the A100](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/final-parking-space/final-parking-space-pair-of-dodge-a100-vans/) . The larger B-Series, with the engine moved forward and a snoutier body shape, debuted as a 1971 model; production of this family of vans continued (with various body updates) all the way through 2003.


Chrysler Corporation


Until the Ram Wagon/Van nomenclature took over in 1981, the B-Series Dodge cargo vans were given Tradesman badging, while the passenger versions were Sportsmen. Plymouth dealers got their own version of the Sportsman for the 1974-1983 model years; this was the origin of the Plymouth Voyager name.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


This van does have some flavor of LA-series two-barrel Chrysler small-block installed, but I don’t think it’s original equipment.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


That’s because the emissions sticker on the valve cover shows a model year of 1978. If the entire engine and not just the valve cover was made for the 1978 model year, it’s either a 318 or a 360. Hauling a load of band members and their gear up and down the steep grades around Boulder and points west would have been brutal on engines.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


There are two more V-8s in the back, one Chrysler LA and one Chevrolet small-block, but I think they were tossed in there by Speedway personnel trying to clear the paths between vehicles.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The transmission is[the optional Torqueflite 727 automatic](https://oldcarbrochures.org/United%20States/Chrysler%20Trucks%20and%20Vans/1976-Trucks-and-Vans/1976-Dodge-Tradesman-Wagons-Brochures/slides/1976_Dodge_Tradesman_Vans-11.html) , rather than the base three-on-the-tree manual. This van would have needed plenty of downshifting in the mountains to keep the brakes from burning up.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


I’m pleased that I have been able to document this piece of Colorado history.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


In theory, this van could be resurrected and put back on the road. How about a food truck conversion?


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


I was excited to find what looked like a faded 1970s beer can in the thistles next to this truck, but it turned out to be a Project Pabst[Blucifer](https://visitdenver.com/blog/post/blucifer-dens-infamous-blue-mustang/) -themed can from 2017.


Would you trade your ’76 Tradesman for all the wood in Woodstock? All the bread in Bakersfield?[All the lobster in Newburg](https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/57042/lobster-newburg/) ?
